item.title: NFC Digital Filing System Development
item.description:
250-750 GBP | Hello,
I’m looking for a software/web developer who could help me turn an idea into a simple, user-friendly platform.
The concept is similar in some ways to NFC digital business cards. With these, a physical NFC card is linked to a unique user profile, which can be opened simply by tapping the card against a smartphone.
My idea would use the same principle, but for storing and accessing documents and images.
Each customer would receive a physical NFC card, also containing a QR code, which I am able to manufacture and programme myself. The card would be linked to that customer’s unique account.
When the customer taps the NFC card against their phone, or scans the QR code, they would be taken directly to their own simple user area. From there, they could:
- Create folders - Upload images, receipts and scanned documents - View and manage previously uploaded files - Organise their files within their account
The key part of the idea is simplicity. I don’t want users to have to remember an email address, username or password. Instead, access would be through a unique link/token associated with their physical NFC/QR card.
Ideally, without the card or its unique link, there would be no straightforward way of accessing the account.
From an admin side, I would need to be able to create and manage customer accounts, associate each account with an NFC/QR card, and potentially manage an annual subscription for the service.
I can handle the manufacture, printing and programming of the physical NFC/QR cards, so I’m mainly looking for someone who can develop the web/software side of the project.
The files being stored would primarily be things such as receipts, photographs and scanned documents rather than highly sensitive information. However, I would still want the platform to follow sensible security and data-protection practices.
The purpose of this platform is to allow vehicle enthusiasts to securely upload and store their vehicle’s data—such as invoices, receipts, repair bills, service history—in one location that can then be sold along with the vehicle. This eliminates missing information even if the NFC card is lost since hidden NFC labels could also be placed in vehicles as backups. This ensures transparency for buyers while helping avoid issues like stolen vehicles or falsified histories.
I’m initially looking to create a relatively simple MVP rather than an unnecessarily complicated system, with the possibility of developing it further if the concept proves successful. The design should reflect simplicity and intuitiveness akin to "Apple product" aesthetics—clean and user-friendly for all age groups.
Additionally: - Users should start with a fixed storage amount tied to their card but have options to expand storage if needed without incurring high costs on my end. - Attached images are included as references for my vision; these were created using non-specialized software but convey the core idea clearly.
If this sounds like something you could build, please get in touch. I’d be interested to hear how you would approach the project, what technology you would suggest using, an approximate development timescale, and an indication of cost.

Hard to discover trusted local tradespeople.
No simple way to record and verify collaborations across projects.
Low retention for community platforms without a daily habit.
Merchants need a place to be rated and discovered by local trades.

Small merchants and suppliers who want ratings and local visibility.
Local customers searching for trusted trades within a radius.
Community managers / local trade associations who want to promote verified professionals.

Profile pages: portfolio gallery, trade tags, average collaboration score, contact CTA.
Radius Forum: create posts, filter by trade and distance, comment, flag content.
Merchant listings & reviews: create merchant entries, submit ratings and comments, recalc averages.
Daily puzzle widget: embedded iframe; webhook endpoint to record completions and award points/badges.
Basic gamification: points, streaks, badges, leaderboard placeholder.
Admin tools: flagged content queue, revoke points, basic metrics.
Phase 2 (after validation) Invite collaborators: send/accept invites, create CollaborationRecord, optional peer ratings.
Verification badge: awarded when collaborators confirm and meet criteria.
Reference requests: contact flow to request references from collaborators.
Dispute resolution: admin tools for disputes and rating moderation.
Growth loop: invite tracking, referral rewards, featured merchant placements.
4. Pages and reusable elements (Bubble names) Pages: Home, Newsfeed, RadiusForum, Profile, MerchantDirectory, PuzzleModal, AdminDashboard, InviteInbox.
Reusable elements: PuzzleCard, PuzzleModal (iframe), ProfileCard, CollaborationCard, BadgeShelf, InviteModal, MerchantCard, FlagModal.

ForumPost: author, trade, radius_miles, content, created_at, flags.
Merchant: name, location, rating_avg, reviews.
PuzzleEmbedLog: user, provider, action, timestamp, idempotency_key.
CollaborationRecord: title, initiator, collaborators, photos, start_date, end_date, ratings, is_verified.
Invite: token, sender, recipient, status, sent_at, responded_at.
6. Key workflows (developer‑ready) Onboarding: create User → email verify → prompt portfolio upload → set location.
Open puzzle: PuzzleCard → open PuzzleModal (iframe with user_id & idempotency token).
Puzzle webhook: verify HMAC/timestamp → idempotency check → create PuzzleEmbedLog → award points/badges (one per day).
Create forum post: create ForumPost → notify users within radius.
Invite collaborator: create Invite → send email + in‑app notification → accept adds CollaborationRecord and updates both profiles.
Merchant review: create review → recalc Merchant.rating_avg.
7. Acceptance criteria & KPIs Acceptance criteria
Puzzle webhook validates HMAC and enforces one completion per user per day.
Invite accept flow updates both profiles within 3s and allows optional rating.
Admin can view flagged items and revoke points/badges.
KPIs
DAU, 7‑day retention, puzzle completion rate, invite conversion (sent→accepted), new users via invites, verified collaboration rate.
8. Suggested build approach & timeline Phase approach: MVP core (2–6 weeks with Bubble specialist), soft launch to 50–200 users, measure KPIs, then Phase 2.
Tech choice: Bubble for MVP (fast, low cost). Custom webhook endpoint (small Node/Express or serverless) for secure HMAC verification and idempotency.
Budget guidance: freelancer Bubble build £4k–£8k; small agency £10k–£20k depending on polish and Phase 2 scope.

Filter & subscribe: filter by region (e.g., UK regions), business size, and sector (construction, home services). Users can subscribe to email alerts for new grants.

Grant alerts: push or email alerts for grants closing within 14 days.
UX notes Place the News & Grants section on the main navigation and surface urgent grants on the dashboard.
Use cards with clear CTAs (“Read more”, “Check eligibility”, “Save for later”).
Allow merchants to sponsor a grant highlight for visibility (monetisation option).
10. Example grant types to include (what to curate) Local enterprise grants (county or city business support funds).
SME growth grants (innovation, digital adoption, equipment purchase).

Green retrofit or energy efficiency grants (for trades doing retrofit work).

11. How to keep the Grants feed accurate (operational) Sources: UK government portals, local council business pages, Local Enterprise Partnerships (LEPs), Innovate UK, British Business Bank, and trade association bulletins.
Curation process: admin reviews and approves new grant entries; set a 30‑day recheck for each grant to ensure links and deadlines are current.
Automation: use RSS or API feeds where available; otherwise, manual curation with scheduled reminders.
12. Example News & Grants content items (templates) Grant card: Title; 1‑line summary; Eligibility tags; Deadline; CTA link; “Save” icon.
News update: Headline; 2–3 sentence summary; link to full article; related grants.
Success story: Profile of a tradesperson who used a grant; before/after photos; grant used; contact for mentorship.
